controlled_next_step.bounded_experiment: One separately prepared/admitted diagnostic attempt using the same three whole files, all original numerical/cost checks, fixtures, warmups, three alternating measured pairs and strict thresholds. Apply exactly one unconditional GC.gc(true) preparation to each of the four named cases (UPR RBig C residual/outer and DUAL RBig update lower/free), after all existing warmups/wrapper checks and before the first measured pair, with both fixture sides retained. No collection between arms or pairs. Fix these sites before examining outcomes.
controlled_next_step.controls: Exact inverse for the added preparation/logging blocks, immutable prior failure records, fresh host/ref/resource admission and single-attempt clock. No batch tuning, threshold changes, sample changes, order changes, repeated collection until pass, library overrides or production optimization.
controlled_next_step.hypothesis: Prior garbage and finalizer/native allocator state after extensive correctness and warmup work contributes to variability of the charged capacity metric; one fixed post-warmup full collection may reduce that sensitivity.
controlled_next_step.interpretation: Treat an improvement as evidence of preparation sensitivity only; a failure leaves the hypothesis unconfirmed. Neither result alone warrants release or a general claim of deterministic allocator behavior. Any permanent test change needs review and complete qualification with all original checks.
controlled_next_step.recording: Record each collection as a separate preparation cost with elapsed, bytes/events, compile/recompile, GC time and raw GC counters where available; never merge preparation into or subtract it from whole-function measured costs. Preserve all named pair/metadata data and ordinary root Test status.
controlled_next_step.why_targeted: The measured routines/fixtures are unchanged, event savings persist, bytes vary with fixed event components and no in-window GC, and the current runtime explicitly counts usable native capacity. BigInt finalizers give an actual mechanism by which preparation affects allocator state.

not_proven: No allocation-level requested-size/address/usable-size trace was captured, so we cannot attribute every byte difference to malloc capacity or prove an identical native request sequence from aggregate counters alone.
No in-window GC explanation is supported for these failures.
No causal proof ties prior unreachable objects or collection history to these byte failures; those are testable preparation-state hypotheses.
Equal checksums and event counts do not by themselves prove identical full numerical trajectories, retained-memory use, or elapsed performance.
A later passing run would not retroactively prove the original cause or erase either failed run.
proved: The two current gate failures are byte predicates, not missing event savings.
DUAL event components remain constant within each method while bytes vary between its three samples.
No collection pause, full sweep or GC time was recorded inside DUAL measured windows; UPR recorded GC seconds0 but did not capture raw pause/full_sweep fields.
The runtime byte metric includes native usable capacity and positive realloc capacity changes; equal event counts do not imply equal requested sizes or equal usable bytes.
The changed epsilon/bound/auxiliary kernels are not directly called by the unchanged measured residual/update functions, as established by the bound prior source reviews.

scope: Bounded source-and-counter diagnosis; acceptance means the analysis is supported, not that original causes are proved or any failing test is waived

source_attribution.GC_preparation_semantics: Installed gcutils.jl documents full collection traversing live objects and reclaiming unreachable objects; BigInt finalizers connect object lifetime to native limb allocation lifetime. This supplies a plausible state-changing intervention, not proof that a particular collection will canonicalize malloc state.
source_attribution.installed_Base_timing: timing.jl:gc_total_bytes adds allocd,deferred_alloc,total_allocd; GC_Diff takes differences; @timed bytes=diff.allocd. Events sum malloc,realloc,poolalloc,bigalloc. These are accounting counters, not a trace of requested payload sizes or abstract arithmetic operations.
source_attribution.installed_GMP: gmp.jl:BigInt construction registers __gmpz_clear finalizer. GMP initialization installs jl_gc_counted_malloc, jl_gc_counted_realloc_with_old_size and jl_gc_counted_free_with_size callbacks.
source_attribution.native_free: upstream-gc-stock.c3893: free releases block and adjusts free pressure; it does not subtract from cumulative allocated-byte total.
source_attribution.native_malloc: upstream-gc-stock.c3859-3874 and saved matching native disassembly: counted malloc calls malloc(requested), then charges memory_block_usable_size(data) to allocd and increments malloc event count.
source_attribution.native_realloc: upstream-gc-stock.c3901 onward: counted realloc charges only nonnegative difference between returned usable size and supplied old size, and increments realloc count.
source_attribution.runtime_provenance: 12 selected native/source/disassembly hashes independently rechecked against saved S4-O source-attribution.json, including current libjulia-internal, libjulia, libc, timing.jl, native allocation wrappers and usable-size disassembly. No S4-O script rerun.
source_attribution.usable_capacity: upstream-gc-common.c137 and current-runtime-bound disassembly: this Linux memory_block_usable_size path calls malloc_usable_size. Returned capacity can exceed requested payload; counter bytes cannot be equated with requested sizes.

work_memory_review: No new production work or retention is proposed. A full collection scans live objects and can run finalizers; that preparation is materially costly and must be reported separately. It is justified here only as one bounded diagnostic intervention, not an unmeasured hot-path remedy.
